framework.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) v2.0
framework.description: NIST CSF 2.0 organises cybersecurity outcomes into 6 Functions (Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover), 22 Categories and 106 Subcategories, crosswalked here to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.
framework.author: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)

controls.title: The organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
controls.description: The organisation's mission and objectives are stated plainly enough that cybersecurity decisions can be traced back to them, so risk is judged by its effect on what the organisation exists to do rather than in the abstract.
evidence_checklist: Published mission or strategy statement currently in force
Record linking cybersecurity objectives to specific mission outcomes
Evidence the link is revisited when the mission or strategy changes

controls.title: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood and considered
controls.description: The parties with a stake in the organisation's cybersecurity are identified along with what each expects, so requirements are gathered deliberately rather than arriving as complaints or audit findings.
evidence_checklist: Stakeholder register naming internal and external parties
Recorded cybersecurity expectations per stakeholder group
Evidence those expectations were considered in a risk or planning decision

controls.title: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity, including privacy and civil liberties obligations, are understood and managed
controls.description: Every statutory, regulatory and contractual cybersecurity obligation the organisation is subject to is identified, owned and tracked, privacy obligations included, so compliance is a managed position rather than an assumption.
evidence_checklist: Register of applicable laws, regulations and contractual security clauses
Named owner and current status against each obligation
Record of the most recent legal or regulatory review

controls.title: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organization are understood and communicated
controls.description: The services others rely on the organisation to deliver are identified and their criticality agreed, so protection and recovery effort is spent where an outage would be felt outside the organisation.
evidence_checklist: Business impact analysis identifying externally depended-upon services
Agreed criticality or service tiering
Evidence the criticality decisions were communicated to service owners

controls.title: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are understood and communicated
controls.description: The external services, suppliers and infrastructure the organisation itself depends on are identified and the effect of their loss understood, so inherited risk is visible before an outage discovers it.
evidence_checklist: Dependency map covering suppliers, platforms and utilities
Impact assessment for loss of each critical dependency
Evidence dependencies are reviewed on a defined cycle

controls.title: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
controls.description: What the cybersecurity risk programme is trying to achieve is written down and agreed by the people accountable for it, so later disagreements about priority have a documented reference.
evidence_checklist: Documented cybersecurity risk management objectives
Record of stakeholder agreement or approval
Evidence objectives are reviewed at planned intervals

controls.title: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained
controls.description: The amount of cybersecurity risk the organisation will accept is stated in terms specific enough to decide a real case, and kept current, so acceptance decisions are consistent between teams.
evidence_checklist: Approved risk appetite and risk tolerance statements
Evidence of communication to risk owners and decision makers
Record of the most recent review or revision

controls.title: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes
controls.description: Cybersecurity risk sits in the same register, on the same scale and reported through the same route as the organisation's other risks, so it can be compared and traded off against them.
evidence_checklist: Enterprise risk register showing cybersecurity entries
Evidence cyber risks use the enterprise scoring scale
Board or executive risk report containing cybersecurity items

controls.title: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated
controls.description: The organisation states which responses (accept, mitigate, transfer, avoid) are appropriate in which circumstances, so risk owners are not each inventing a policy at the point of decision.
evidence_checklist: Documented risk response strategy and decision criteria
Evidence of communication to risk owners
Examples of response decisions recorded against the criteria

controls.title: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties
controls.description: Named routes exist for raising and escalating cybersecurity risk, including risk originating with suppliers, so a concern reaches a decision maker without depending on who happens to know whom.
evidence_checklist: Documented escalation and reporting paths with named roles
Evidence third-party risk uses the same routes
Examples of risks escalated through the documented path

controls.title: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated
controls.description: One risk method is used across the organisation, so two teams assessing comparable exposures arrive at comparable scores and the register can be ranked meaningfully.
evidence_checklist: Documented risk assessment methodology with scoring scales
Evidence the method is applied in current risk assessments
Record of training or communication of the method

controls.title: Strategic opportunities (i.e., positive risks) are characterized and are included in organizational cybersecurity risk discussions
controls.description: Opportunities a security investment would open up - new markets, new assurance claims, retired legacy cost - are recorded alongside threats, so risk discussion is not only about loss avoidance.
evidence_checklist: Register or minutes recording cybersecurity opportunities
Evidence opportunities are assessed with the same method as threats
Example of an opportunity carried into a planning or budget decision

controls.title: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving
controls.description: Accountability for cybersecurity risk sits with named leaders rather than with the security function alone, and their conduct visibly supports the behaviour the policy asks of everyone else.
evidence_checklist: Terms of reference or charter assigning leadership accountability
Minutes showing leadership review of cybersecurity risk
Evidence of leadership communication on security culture

controls.title: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced
controls.description: Every cybersecurity duty has a named holder with the authority to discharge it, conflicting duties are separated, and the assignment is known to the people it binds.
evidence_checklist: RACI or equivalent covering cybersecurity duties
Evidence of segregation between conflicting duties
Evidence role holders were informed and acknowledged the assignment

controls.title: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies
controls.description: Budget, headcount and tooling are allocated in proportion to the risk strategy the organisation has adopted, so policy commitments are funded rather than aspirational.
evidence_checklist: Approved cybersecurity budget and staffing plan
Evidence resourcing was justified against the risk strategy
Record of resource gaps raised and their disposition

controls.title: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices
controls.description: Screening, terms of employment, awareness, disciplinary process and offboarding all carry cybersecurity obligations, so the personnel lifecycle enforces them rather than relying on separate reminders.
evidence_checklist: Employment terms containing security obligations
Screening records appropriate to role sensitivity
Offboarding checklist covering access revocation and asset return

controls.title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced
controls.description: A cybersecurity policy exists, is derived from the organisation's own context rather than a template, is approved at the right level, and is actually applied.
evidence_checklist: Approved cybersecurity policy showing version and approval date
Evidence of publication and communication to those it binds
Examples of the policy being enforced in a real decision

controls.title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organizational mission
controls.description: The policy is revisited on a schedule and after significant change, so it continues to describe how the organisation actually operates rather than how it operated when the policy was written.
evidence_checklist: Policy review schedule and record of the last review
Change log showing revisions and their triggers
Evidence updates were re-communicated

controls.title: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction
controls.description: The results the strategy produced are examined against what it set out to achieve, so direction is set from measured outcomes rather than from activity counts.
evidence_checklist: Review record comparing outcomes against stated objectives
Metrics or KPIs used in the review
Decisions taken as a result of the review

controls.title: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks
controls.description: The strategy is checked for gaps against the organisation's current requirements and risk register, so changes in the business are reflected before they become exposures.
evidence_checklist: Coverage assessment of the strategy against the risk register
Record of identified gaps and remediation plans
Evidence of independent or second-line review

controls.title: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed
controls.description: Programme performance is measured and reviewed by people with the authority to change it, so persistent underperformance results in an adjustment rather than a repeated report.
evidence_checklist: Defined performance measures for the cybersecurity programme
Management review minutes covering those measures
Adjustments made in response to performance findings

controls.title: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
controls.description: Supply chain cybersecurity is run as a named programme with its own objectives and owners, rather than as a clause appearing in individual contracts.
evidence_checklist: Approved supply chain cybersecurity policy or programme charter
Named programme owner and governance forum
Documented processes covering supplier onboarding through exit

controls.title: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally
controls.description: Who is responsible for which control is agreed with each third party and known on both sides, so no control is left assumed to be the other party's job.
evidence_checklist: Responsibility matrix agreed with key suppliers or partners
Evidence the split was communicated to both sides
Named internal owner for each third-party relationship

controls.title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes
controls.description: Supplier risk is assessed, recorded and improved through the same processes as internal risk, so it is ranked against internal exposures rather than tracked separately.
evidence_checklist: Supplier risks present in the enterprise or cyber risk register
Evidence supplier risk uses the standard assessment method
Improvement actions tracked to closure

controls.title: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality
controls.description: A current supplier inventory exists with an agreed criticality rating, so assurance effort is concentrated on the suppliers whose failure would matter most.
evidence_checklist: Supplier inventory with criticality or tier assigned
Documented criteria used to assign criticality
Evidence the inventory is kept current

controls.title: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other types of agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties
controls.description: Security requirements are written into the agreement rather than requested afterwards, so they are enforceable and priced in.
evidence_checklist: Standard security clauses or schedule used in supplier contracts
Sample executed contracts containing the clauses
Evidence requirements are tailored to supplier criticality

controls.title: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships
controls.description: Prospective suppliers are assessed before signature, while the organisation still has the leverage to require change or walk away.
evidence_checklist: Pre-contract due diligence questionnaires or assessment reports
Record of findings and how they were resolved before signature
Approval record for onboarding the supplier

controls.title: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship
controls.description: Supplier risk is re-assessed through the life of the relationship rather than only at onboarding, so a supplier's deterioration is noticed while the contract is still live.
evidence_checklist: Ongoing supplier risk assessments with dates
Monitoring evidence such as assurance reports or attestations
Record of risk responses agreed with the supplier

controls.title: Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities
controls.description: Suppliers whose systems or staff would be involved in an incident are named in the plan and have taken part in exercising it, so first contact is not made during the incident.
evidence_checklist: Incident response plan naming supplier roles and contacts
Evidence suppliers participated in an exercise or test
Agreed notification obligations and timescales

controls.title: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle
controls.description: Supply chain controls are measured and reported like any other control set, across the whole life of the product or service rather than at procurement only.
evidence_checklist: Defined supply chain security measures and reporting cadence
Performance reports covering live supplier relationships
Evidence of action taken when performance fell short

controls.title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement
controls.description: Exit is planned in advance - data return or destruction, access revocation, key rotation, transition support - so ending a relationship does not leave residual access or stranded data.
evidence_checklist: Documented supplier offboarding or exit procedure
Contract provisions covering data return and destruction
Completed offboarding records for a terminated supplier

controls.title: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained
controls.description: A current record of the physical devices the organisation manages exists and is kept current, because no other control can be applied consistently to equipment nobody knows about.
evidence_checklist: Hardware asset inventory with owner and location per device
Documented process and cadence for keeping it current
Reconciliation between the inventory and a discovery scan

controls.title: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
controls.description: A current record of installed software, subscribed services and operated systems exists, so patching, licensing and end-of-life decisions have something to work from.
evidence_checklist: Software and service inventory with version and owner
Documented process for adding and retiring entries
Reconciliation between the inventory and a credentialed collection run

controls.title: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained
controls.description: The communication the organisation intends to permit is documented, so observed traffic and exposed services can be compared against an authorised baseline instead of being judged case by case.
controls.scan_module_hint: Services & Ports / Offline Configuration Scan / Services & Ports
evidence_checklist: Current network diagram showing zones and trust boundaries
Documented authorised flows, including external connections
Evidence observed services were reconciled against the authorised set

controls.title: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained
controls.description: The services the organisation consumes from third parties are inventoried with their owners and data exposure, so supply chain risk has a concrete scope.
evidence_checklist: Inventory of supplier-provided services with internal owner
Data types and systems each service touches
Evidence the inventory is reviewed on a defined cycle

controls.title: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission
controls.description: Assets carry an agreed classification and criticality, so protection effort and incident priority follow business impact rather than technical convenience.
evidence_checklist: Documented classification and criticality scheme
Assets in the inventory carrying an assigned rating
Evidence ratings drive handling or protection decisions

controls.title: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained
controls.description: The organisation knows which designated data types it holds, where they live and who owns them, which is what makes retention, classification and breach scoping possible.
evidence_checklist: Data inventory or record of processing per designated data type
Storage locations and named data owners
Evidence the inventory is refreshed when systems change

controls.title: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles
controls.description: Assets are governed from acquisition to secure disposal, so end-of-life equipment and unsupported software are retired deliberately rather than left in place.
evidence_checklist: Documented asset lifecycle procedure covering acquisition to disposal
Records of secure disposal or media sanitisation
Register of end-of-life or unsupported assets and their plan

controls.title: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
controls.description: Vulnerabilities are found by a repeatable process, confirmed rather than assumed, and recorded so their treatment can be tracked to closure.
evidence_checklist: Recent authenticated vulnerability scan results
Evidence findings were validated rather than accepted from the tool
Vulnerability register showing status and owner

controls.title: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources
controls.description: The organisation subscribes to threat sources relevant to its sector and technology, so it learns about active threats from somewhere other than its own incidents.
evidence_checklist: List of subscribed threat intelligence sources or sharing groups
Evidence intelligence reaches a named recipient and is triaged
Example of intelligence that changed a control or priority

controls.title: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded
controls.description: Threats specific to this organisation - not a generic list - are identified and recorded, so risk assessment starts from a considered threat picture.
evidence_checklist: Threat register or threat assessment covering internal and external actors
Evidence the assessment is specific to the organisation's context
Record of the most recent refresh

controls.title: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded
controls.description: Each credible threat-vulnerability pair carries a recorded impact and likelihood, which is what turns a vulnerability list into something that can be prioritised.
evidence_checklist: Risk assessment records showing impact and likelihood per scenario
Documented basis for the ratings assigned
Evidence assessments are updated as the environment changes

controls.title: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization
controls.description: The recorded factors are combined into an inherent risk position that visibly drives what gets fixed first.
evidence_checklist: Prioritised risk register derived from the assessment inputs
Documented prioritisation criteria
Evidence the priority order drove remediation scheduling

controls.title: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated
controls.description: Each accepted risk has a chosen response with an owner and a date, and progress against it is visible, so treatment is tracked rather than assumed.
evidence_checklist: Risk treatment plan with owners and target dates
Evidence of tracking to closure, including overdue items
Outstanding critical and high vulnerability counts trending down

controls.title: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, recorded, and tracked
controls.description: Changes and approved deviations are assessed for security impact before they land and are recorded with an expiry, so exceptions do not quietly become the standard.
evidence_checklist: Change records showing security impact assessment
Exception register with justification, approver and expiry
Evidence expired exceptions are chased

controls.title: Processes for receiving, analyzing, and responding to vulnerability disclosures are established
controls.description: An external finder has a published, monitored route to report a vulnerability, and reports received that way are triaged like any other finding.
evidence_checklist: Published vulnerability disclosure policy and contact address
Records of disclosures received and their triage
Defined acknowledgement and response timescales

controls.title: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use
controls.description: Hardware and software are checked for authenticity and integrity before deployment - signatures, checksums, trusted sourcing - so tampering is caught before it is trusted.
evidence_checklist: Documented verification procedure for new hardware and software
Evidence of signature or checksum verification for recent acquisitions
Approved-source list or equivalent procurement control

controls.title: Critical suppliers are assessed prior to acquisition
controls.description: Suppliers rated critical are security-assessed before the organisation commits, so a supplier's weaknesses are known while there is still a choice.
evidence_checklist: Pre-acquisition security assessments for critical suppliers
Documented assessment criteria and pass threshold
Approval records referencing the assessment outcome

controls.title: Improvements are identified from evaluations
controls.description: Audits, assessments and self-evaluations produce recorded improvement actions rather than reports that are read and filed.
evidence_checklist: Recent evaluation or audit reports
Improvement actions raised from them, with owners
Evidence actions are tracked to closure

controls.title: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties
controls.description: Penetration tests, tabletop exercises and recovery tests feed a recorded improvement backlog, including where the finding involves a supplier.
evidence_checklist: Reports from recent tests or exercises
Improvement actions traced back to specific test findings
Evidence suppliers were included where relevant

controls.title: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities
controls.description: Day-to-day operation - not only incidents and audits - is treated as a source of improvement, so friction and near-misses are captured while they are still cheap to fix.
evidence_checklist: Mechanism for staff to raise process improvements
Improvement items originating from routine operations
Evidence items are reviewed and dispositioned

controls.title: Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved
controls.description: The plans people are expected to follow under pressure exist, are known to them, and are revised after each use or exercise.
evidence_checklist: Current incident response, continuity and recovery plans
Evidence the plans were distributed to the roles they name
Revision history showing updates after incidents or exercises

controls.category_name: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
controls.title: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization
controls.description: Accounts and credentials for people, services and devices are issued, changed and revoked through a controlled process, with credential strength enforced by configuration rather than by request.
evidence_checklist: Documented joiner, mover and leaver procedure
Enforced password policy showing length and complexity settings
Register of service and machine accounts with owners

controls.category_name: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
controls.title: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions
controls.description: The strength of identity proofing matches what the identity will be able to do, so a privileged account is not issued on the same evidence as a guest one.
evidence_checklist: Documented identity proofing requirements by account type
Records of proofing performed for recent privileged accounts
Evidence proofing strength is reviewed against account privilege

controls.category_name: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
controls.title: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated
controls.description: Access requires authentication appropriate to the risk, with multi-factor authentication where the exposure warrants it, and the settings are verifiable on the host.
evidence_checklist: Authentication policy stating where MFA is required
Host configuration showing enforced authentication settings
Evidence of lockout thresholds on repeated failure

controls.category_name: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
controls.title: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified
controls.description: Tokens, tickets and session assertions are transmitted over protected channels and validated on receipt, so an authenticated session cannot be replayed or forged in transit.
evidence_checklist: Federation or SSO configuration showing signed, encrypted assertions
Evidence assertion transport uses current TLS with strong ciphers
Session validation and expiry settings

controls.category_name: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
controls.title: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
controls.description: Entitlements follow a written policy, grant the least privilege that works, keep incompatible duties apart, and are re-reviewed rather than accumulating.
controls.scan_module_hint: Offline Configuration Scan (access review) / Credential Validation (privileged access, MFA)
evidence_checklist: Access control policy covering least privilege and separation of duties
Evidence of periodic entitlement review with removals actioned
Privileged account list showing restricted membership and MFA

controls.category_name: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
controls.title: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk
controls.description: Physical entry to areas holding sensitive assets is controlled, logged and reviewed in proportion to what those areas contain.
evidence_checklist: Defined secure areas with entry control mechanisms
Access logs for secure areas and evidence of review
Visitor procedure including escort and record keeping

controls.title: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind
controls.description: Everyone receives awareness training appropriate to their work, refreshed on a cycle, and the organisation can show who has completed it.
evidence_checklist: Awareness programme content and schedule
Completion records covering current staff and contractors
Evidence of refresher training on a defined cycle

controls.title: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind
controls.description: People holding security-significant roles get training specific to those duties, beyond the general awareness everyone receives.
evidence_checklist: List of specialised roles and their training requirements
Completion or certification records for role holders
Evidence requirements are revisited as roles change

controls.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
controls.description: Stored data is encrypted or otherwise protected in proportion to its classification, and the protection is verifiable on the host rather than asserted in a policy.
controls.scan_module_hint: Offline Configuration Scan (disk encryption, UAC) / TLS / Certificates
evidence_checklist: Encryption standard stating where data-at-rest encryption is required
Host evidence that volume or disk encryption is enabled
Key management procedure covering storage and rotation

controls.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected
controls.description: Data crossing a network is carried over current, correctly configured transport encryption, and legacy protocols that would silently downgrade it are disabled.
controls.scan_module_hint: Services & Ports / Offline Configuration Scan / Services & Ports / TLS / Certificates
evidence_checklist: Transport encryption standard naming permitted protocol versions
Certificate inventory showing validity and issuer
Host evidence that legacy TLS and cleartext services are disabled

controls.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected
controls.description: Data being processed in memory is protected from other tenants and processes, through isolation, controlled privilege escalation, masking or equivalent measures.
evidence_checklist: Documented controls protecting data during processing
Evidence of memory or tenant isolation on shared platforms
Data masking or minimisation applied in non-production use

controls.title: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested
controls.description: Backups are taken on a defined schedule, protected against the same event that would take out production, and proven by restore tests rather than by the backup job reporting success.
evidence_checklist: Backup policy stating scope, frequency and retention
Evidence backups are protected and held separately from production
Results of the most recent restore test

controls.title: Configuration management practices are established and applied
controls.description: Systems are built and kept to a documented secure baseline, and drift from it is detectable, so hardening is a maintained state rather than a build-day event.
evidence_checklist: Documented hardening baselines per platform
Host evidence that baseline settings are in force
Process for detecting and correcting configuration drift

controls.title: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
controls.description: Software is patched, upgraded or removed on a timescale set by risk, and the outstanding position is measurable rather than anecdotal.
evidence_checklist: Patch policy with remediation timescales by severity
Current outstanding critical and high vulnerability counts
Register of unsupported software with a removal plan

controls.title: Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
controls.description: Hardware is maintained, refreshed and disposed of on a risk-driven schedule, with end-of-support equipment tracked and retired rather than left running.
evidence_checklist: Hardware maintenance and refresh schedule
Register of end-of-support hardware with replacement plans
Secure disposal records for retired equipment

controls.title: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring
controls.description: Systems generate the log records monitoring depends on, keep them long enough to be useful, and make them reachable by the people and tools that analyse them.
controls.scan_module_hint: Offline Configuration Scan (audit policy, log retention) / Offline Configuration Scan (NTP)
evidence_checklist: Audit and logging policy naming required event types
Host evidence that audit policy is configured and retention is set
Evidence logs reach a central collector or reviewer

controls.title: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented
controls.description: Only approved software can be installed or run, enforced technically where possible, so unapproved and unmanaged code does not reach production systems.
evidence_checklist: Software allow-list or approval process
Technical enforcement configuration where applied
Evidence of periodic review for unauthorised installations

controls.title: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle
controls.description: Security is built into how software is specified, written, reviewed and released, and the effectiveness of those practices is measured rather than assumed.
evidence_checklist: Secure development policy covering the full lifecycle
Evidence of security testing in the pipeline and its results
Separation between development, test and production environments

controls.title: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage
controls.description: Network access is restricted to what is authorised, environments are segregated, and the exposed service surface matches the intended design.
controls.scan_module_hint: Services & Ports / Offline Configuration Scan / Services & Ports
evidence_checklist: Network segmentation design showing zones and permitted flows
Firewall or access control rule set with review evidence
Host evidence that unnecessary and legacy services are not listening

controls.title: The organization's technology assets are protected from environmental threats
controls.description: Facilities holding technology assets are protected against fire, flood, power loss and similar physical hazards appropriate to their location.
evidence_checklist: Environmental risk assessment for facilities holding assets
Evidence of protective measures such as fire suppression and UPS
Maintenance and test records for those measures

controls.title: Mechanisms are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations
controls.description: Redundancy and failover exist where the recovery objectives require them, and have been proven under conditions resembling an actual failure.
evidence_checklist: Documented availability and recovery objectives per service
Design evidence of redundancy or failover for those services
Results of the most recent failover or continuity test

controls.title: Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained
controls.description: Compute, storage and network capacity are monitored against demand and provisioned ahead of it, so availability is not lost to predictable exhaustion.
evidence_checklist: Capacity monitoring covering compute, storage and network
Defined thresholds and the escalation they trigger
Capacity forecast or plan supporting the next planning period

controls.title: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
controls.description: Network traffic and services are watched by a mechanism capable of raising an alert, so adverse activity is noticed by the organisation rather than reported to it.
evidence_checklist: Network monitoring or IDS/IPS coverage across monitored segments
Host evidence that detection agents are present and running
Records of alerts raised and triaged

controls.title: The physical environment is monitored to find potentially adverse events
controls.description: Physical spaces holding sensitive assets are monitored, and what the monitoring records is actually reviewed.
evidence_checklist: Physical monitoring coverage such as CCTV or intrusion detection
Evidence of review of physical monitoring records
Procedure for responding to a physical alarm

controls.title: Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events
controls.description: User and administrator activity is logged and reviewed for signs of misuse or compromise, within the bounds the organisation has told staff about.
controls.scan_module_hint: Offline Configuration Scan (audit policy, log retention)
evidence_checklist: Host evidence that user and privileged activity auditing is enabled
Log retention meeting the stated policy
Evidence of review, alerting or anomaly detection on that activity

controls.title: External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
controls.description: What providers do inside the organisation's environment is monitored to the same standard as internal activity, rather than trusted on the basis of the contract.
evidence_checklist: Monitoring coverage over provider access and provider-run services
Evidence provider activity is logged and reviewed
Provider assurance reports and how they are checked

controls.title: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events
controls.description: Endpoints and servers carry monitoring that can detect malicious code and unauthorised change to files and configuration.
controls.scan_module_hint: Malware Scan / Offline Configuration Scan (IDS/EDR presence)
evidence_checklist: Host evidence that anti-malware or EDR is installed and active
File integrity or configuration monitoring coverage
Records of detections and how they were handled

controls.title: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities
controls.description: Alerts are analysed by someone or something able to establish what actually happened, so raw detections become findings rather than a queue.
evidence_checklist: Documented triage and analysis procedure
Evidence detection tooling is deployed and feeding the analysis
Analysis records for a sample of recent events

controls.title: Information is correlated from multiple sources
controls.description: Events from different systems are brought together so activity spanning more than one host or control can be seen as one sequence.
controls.scan_module_hint: Offline Configuration Scan (audit policy, log retention)
evidence_checklist: List of log sources feeding a central collector
Host evidence that auditing and retention support correlation
Example of a finding that required more than one source

controls.title: The estimated impact and scope of adverse events are understood
controls.description: Each adverse event carries an assessment of what it reached and what it affected, which is what determines the response it receives.
evidence_checklist: Impact and scope assessment recorded per significant event
Documented criteria used to assess scope
Evidence monitoring coverage is sufficient to establish scope

controls.title: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools
controls.description: Detections reach the people and systems that can act on them, on a timescale that still allows action.
evidence_checklist: Alert routing configuration naming recipients or channels
Evidence detection output reaches those recipients
Records showing acknowledgement and response times

controls.title: Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information are integrated into the analysis
controls.description: Threat intelligence and asset context are available to the analysis step, so an alert is judged against what is known about the threat and the asset.
evidence_checklist: Threat intelligence feeds integrated into detection or analysis
Evidence asset criticality is available to analysts
Example of intelligence changing the disposition of an alert

controls.title: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria
controls.description: Written criteria decide when an event becomes an incident, so declaration is consistent rather than dependent on who is on shift.
evidence_checklist: Documented incident declaration criteria and severity levels
Evidence the criteria were applied to recent events
Record of criteria review after incidents or exercises

controls.title: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared
controls.description: Declaring an incident starts a documented plan that names roles and third-party involvement, so response follows a plan rather than being improvised.
evidence_checklist: Current incident response plan with named roles
Execution records or after-action reports from a real incident
Third-party contacts and their agreed involvement

controls.title: Incident reports are triaged and validated
controls.description: Reports are checked and confirmed before response effort is committed, so false reports are filtered and genuine ones are not dismissed.
evidence_checklist: Documented triage and validation procedure
Triage records showing the validation decision
Defined triage timescales and evidence they are met

controls.title: Incidents are categorized and prioritized
controls.description: Incidents receive a category and priority from published criteria, so response effort matches severity consistently.
evidence_checklist: Incident categorisation and severity matrix
Recent incidents showing assigned category and priority
Evidence priority drove the response actually given

controls.title: Incidents are escalated or elevated as needed
controls.description: Defined triggers escalate an incident to more senior or specialist responders, so a response that is not working is raised rather than persisted with.
evidence_checklist: Documented escalation criteria and escalation path
Records of incidents escalated and when
Evidence escalation contacts are current

controls.title: The criteria for initiating incident recovery are applied
controls.description: Recovery starts on stated criteria rather than on impatience, so systems are not restored while the cause is still present.
evidence_checklist: Documented criteria for moving from response to recovery
Records showing the criteria were applied to a real incident
Named authority for the recovery decision

controls.title: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident
controls.description: Investigation establishes the sequence of events and the underlying cause, so remediation addresses the cause rather than the symptom.
controls.scan_module_hint: Offline Configuration Scan (audit policy, log retention)
evidence_checklist: Investigation records establishing timeline and root cause
Log sources and retention sufficient to reconstruct the timeline
Corrective actions traced to the identified cause

controls.title: Actions performed during an investigation are recorded, and the records' integrity and provenance are preserved
controls.description: What responders did, when and on whose authority is recorded in a form that stands up later, so the response itself can be reviewed or relied on as evidence.
controls.scan_module_hint: Offline Configuration Scan (audit policy, log retention)
evidence_checklist: Investigation action log with timestamps and actor
Host evidence that audit logging and retention are configured
Controls protecting those records from alteration

controls.title: Incident data and metadata are collected, and their integrity and provenance are preserved
controls.description: Evidence is collected and handled so that its origin and integrity can be demonstrated, which is what makes it usable in a legal or regulatory process.
controls.scan_module_hint: Offline Configuration Scan (audit policy, log retention)
evidence_checklist: Evidence handling and chain-of-custody procedure
Collected artefacts with hashes or equivalent integrity proof
Log retention sufficient to cover the investigation window

controls.title: An incident's magnitude is estimated and validated
controls.description: How far an incident actually reached is estimated and then confirmed, so notification, recovery and reporting decisions rest on a checked figure rather than a first impression.
evidence_checklist: Recorded magnitude or scope estimate per significant incident
Evidence the estimate was validated against collected data
Post-incident review confirming or correcting the estimate

controls.title: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents
controls.description: The parties who need to know are told within the timescales the organisation is bound to, including regulators and affected individuals where that applies.
evidence_checklist: Notification matrix naming parties and statutory timescales
Records of notifications sent for recent incidents
Evidence contact details are kept current

controls.title: Information is shared with designated internal and external stakeholders
controls.description: Incident information is shared with the designated recipients - including sharing communities where relevant - under rules that control what may be disclosed.
evidence_checklist: Information sharing policy including handling restrictions
Records of information shared and with whom
Membership of any sharing community relied upon

controls.title: Incidents are contained
controls.description: Containment stops the incident spreading while preserving what the investigation will need, which is a trade-off that has to be decided deliberately.
evidence_checklist: Documented containment options and decision criteria
Records of containment actions taken and their timing
Evidence containment preserved required evidence

controls.title: Incidents are eradicated
controls.description: The cause and any attacker foothold are removed and their absence confirmed, so recovery does not restore the problem along with the service.
evidence_checklist: Eradication actions recorded per incident
Host evidence that malicious code protection is active and clean
Verification that the cause is no longer present

controls.title: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process
controls.description: Recovery runs from a written plan that the response process hands over to, so restoration is ordered rather than opportunistic.
evidence_checklist: Recovery plan with defined roles and sequence
Records of recovery execution for a real incident or test
Evidence the handover from response to recovery was authorised

controls.title: Recovery actions are selected, scoped, prioritized, and performed
controls.description: Which systems come back, in what order and to what state is decided against business priority rather than technical convenience.
evidence_checklist: Recovery prioritisation based on service criticality
Recovery runbooks or scoped action lists
Records showing the order actually followed

controls.title: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration
controls.description: Backups and images are checked before they are trusted, so a compromised or corrupt restore point is not the thing that comes back.
evidence_checklist: Backup integrity verification procedure
Verification records from the most recent restore or test
Evidence restore points are checked against the incident timeline

controls.title: Critical mission functions and cybersecurity risk management are considered to establish post-incident operational norms
controls.description: The state the organisation returns to is chosen deliberately, taking account of mission needs and the risk position the incident revealed.
evidence_checklist: Record of the agreed post-incident operating state
Evidence mission priorities informed that decision
Risk decisions carried forward from the incident

controls.title: The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed
controls.description: Restored systems are checked for integrity and monitored before being declared normal, so a clean restoration is demonstrated rather than assumed.
evidence_checklist: Post-restoration integrity verification records
Host evidence that monitoring is active on restored systems
Sign-off confirming return to normal operating status

controls.title: The end of incident recovery is declared based on criteria, and incident-related documentation is completed
controls.description: Recovery is formally closed against stated criteria and the record is completed, so the incident has a defined end and a usable history.
evidence_checklist: Documented criteria for declaring recovery complete
Closure records and completed incident documentation
Post-incident review referencing the closed record

controls.title: Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders
controls.description: Stakeholders are kept informed of recovery progress on an agreed cadence, so the organisation controls the account of its own recovery.
evidence_checklist: Recovery communication plan naming audiences and cadence
Records of updates issued during a real incident or exercise
Evidence contact lists are current

controls.title: Public updates on incident recovery are shared using approved methods and messaging
controls.description: Public statements go out through approved channels and approved wording, so external communication is accurate and consistent under pressure.
evidence_checklist: Approved public communication procedure and spokespersons
Pre-approved message templates or holding statements
Records of public updates issued and their approval
